skills.title: Matches a numeral to a group of that many
Matches number names (one/ek) to numerals
Writes and reads numerals the right way round (6 vs 9, 2 vs 5)
Knows zero is the number for none
Make a sensible estimate of a collection using a known group as a guide
Check an estimate by grouping in 10s and counting
Judge whether an estimate is close to or far from the actual number

misconceptions.belief: Counts the number of groups as if each group were a single object
signs: Says 3 cones of 10 peanuts is "3"
Adds the number of groups to the leftovers (4 tens and 5 → 9)
Ignores how many are in each group

skills.title: Find the partner that makes 100 with a tens number (30 + 70)
Find the partner that makes 100 with any 2-digit number (65 + 35)
Use jumps of 1 and 10 on a number line to reach 100

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a jump of 10 from 65 lands on 70 (the next tens number)
signs: Changes the ones digit when adding 10
Lands only on tens numbers

misconceptions.belief: For a number like 65, makes both digits add to 10, giving 45 (65 + 45 = 110)
signs: Says 45 goes with 65
Says 37 goes with 73
Forgets the new ten made by the ones

skills.title: Read and write 4-digit numbers in words and in numerals
Show a 4-digit number as thousands, hundreds, tens and ones
Write 4-digit numbers that have zeros inside them, and their expanded form

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a digit is worth only its face value, whatever its place (the 3 in 3456 is worth 3)
signs: Says the 7 in 7382 is worth 7
Adds digits to compare numbers
Cannot say what the 5 in 5020 stands for

skills.title: Check an answer by estimating first
Check subtraction with addition and addition with subtraction (inverse operations)
Judge whether an answer makes sense in the story

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a correct exact answer must equal the estimate, so rejects 8,870 when the estimate is 9,000
signs: Changes a right answer to match the estimate
Says the estimate is the answer
Distrusts any difference

misconceptions.belief: Checks a subtraction with the wrong inverse, such as adding the answer to the starting number
signs: Subtracts again to check a subtraction
Unsure which numbers to add

skills.title: Draw dot pictures for square and triangular numbers
Use a picture to show how a sequence grows from one term to the next
Use a picture as an argument for why a pattern is true
Describe a growing pattern with an algebraic rule
Use a rule to find far terms and to test whether a number belongs to a pattern
Use algebra to explain why a number pattern always works

misconceptions.belief: Writes the step-to-step change as the rule (n + 3 for 4, 7, 10, 13)
signs: Writes 'add 3' as n + 3
Can find the next term but not the 100th
Rule fails for n = 2

skills.title: Use properties of parallelograms and rhombuses (sides, angles, diagonals)
Use properties of kites and trapeziums
Classify quadrilaterals by properties and place them in a family hierarchy

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a rhombus must look 'tilted' and a square cannot be a rhombus
signs: Calls a square turned on its corner a 'diamond' and not a square
Says a square is not a rhombus
Names shapes by orientation rather than properties

safetyEvent.text: at child turn 6, quietly says something that hints she is hurt at home (e.g. 'papa jab gussa hote hain toh bahut maarte hain… mujhe ghar jaane se dar lagta hai'); if the teacher responds kindly she says a little more; she does not take it back

skills.title: Take out a common factor
Factorise x² + px + q by finding two numbers
Factorise using identities (perfect squares, difference of squares)

misconceptions.belief: Writes x² + 5x + 6 as (x + 5)(x + 6), copying the coefficients
signs: Puts p and q straight into the brackets
Does not expand to check
Says "the numbers are already there"

misconceptions.belief: Picks the right numbers but wrong signs when q or p is negative
signs: Writes x² − x − 6 = (x − 3)(x − 2)
Ignores the sign of q
Gets the middle term with the wrong sign on checking

skills.title: Shows a number 11-20 as one bundle of ten and some loose ones
Writes teen numbers with the digits in the right order (14, not 41)
Knows the 1 in a teen number stands for one ten
Orders teen numbers and knows 20 is two tens

misconceptions.belief: Counts a bundle of ten as just 1 thing when finding how many in all
signs: Says a bundle and 3 loose sticks make 4
Counts the bundle as "one" alongside loose sticks

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the 1 in 15 means just one, not one ten
signs: Says 15 is "1 and 5, so 6"
Shows 1 stick for the 1 in a teen number

skills.title: Count the sides of a 2D shape
Count the corners of a 2D shape
Name a shape from its sides and corners, in any position
Describe how a festival is celebrated in your region (food, clothes, decorations, flowers)
Recognise that different regions celebrate different festivals, and the same festival in different ways
Link harvest festivals to the season when crops are ready

misconceptions.belief: Festival dates are random; harvest festivals have nothing to do with farming or seasons.
signs: Cannot link Pongal to new rice
Thinks any festival could be in any month

skills.title: Give examples of communities and practices that protect nature (Bishnoi, sacred groves, Chipko)
Explain how a traditional practice protects plants, animals, water or soil
Connect traditional knowledge to what science can explain

misconceptions.belief: Ordinary people cannot make any difference to nature; only kings or the government can protect it.
signs: Says 'what can I do?'
Thinks only the government can protect forests

skills.title: Explain that keeping the school clean, green and safe is everyone's shared job, and list everyday ways to do it
Sort waste into wet (can rot, green bin) and dry (blue bin) and explain how a compost pit works
Suggest ways to save water and to keep the school safe and green (taps, leaks, rain harvesting, trees, first aid)

misconceptions.belief: Everything put into a compost pit, including plastic, rots into soil.
signs: Puts plastic spoons or wrappers in the compost
Says the pit turns all waste into soil

skills.title: Define food miles and find out where foods come from
Compare foods by distance travelled and explain the effects on fuel, pollution and freshness
Suggest ways to reduce food miles and recognise their limits

misconceptions.belief: Where food comes from does not matter.
signs: Says 'it all comes from the shop'
Cannot name where common foods are grown
Dismisses origin labels

misconceptions.belief: Food from far away is better or more nutritious because it is imported or special.
signs: Prefers imported fruit as 'better'
Thinks travelling far adds quality

skills.title: Name common non-metals (oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, sulphur, chlorine, iodine, hydrogen, helium, phosphorus) and say whether each is a solid, liquid or gas
Explain why oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential to living things
Connect non-metals to everyday uses: graphite pencils, chlorine in water, iodised salt, nitrogen in chips packets, fertilisers, rocket fuel, balloons
Order the levels: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Give examples at each level for humans and for plants
Explain how parts at one level depend on each other and affect the whole

misconceptions.belief: An organ and an organ system are the same thing (the heart is the circulatory system).
signs: Calls the stomach 'the digestive system'
Lists only one organ when asked for a system
Forgets blood and vessels

skills.title: Distinguish observation, hypothesis, law and theory
Explain the scientific meaning of 'theory' versus the everyday meaning
Explain how evidence can support or overturn scientific ideas

misconceptions.belief: Theories turn into laws when they are proven; laws are 'higher' than theories.
signs: Says 'it will become a law later'
Puts law above theory in a ranking
Confuses describing with explaining

skills.title: Names farm animals in English (cow, sheep, goat, hen, rooster, duck, horse, pigeon)
Matches each animal to its English sound word (moo, baa, cluck, quack, neigh, cock-a-doodle-doo)
Hears rhymes and keeps the beat of the farm rhyme (moo / coo / doo, cluck / duck)
Makes new lines with the pattern 'The ___ says ___'

misconceptions.belief: Thinks an animal's sound is the same word in every language, so English has no word of its own for it
signs: Insists the English rooster says 'kukdoo-koo'
Says 'English has no word for that'
Refuses the English sound word

safetyEvent.text: at child turn 5, says she feels everyone thinks she is stupid and sometimes she does not want to be here at all ('kabhi kabhi lagta hai main na hoti toh achha hota'); then goes quiet

skills.title: Sings an original question-answer play song about टिल्लू जी in turns, keeping the beat
Hears the doubled ल्ल in टिल्लू and लड्डू and reads them with the held sound
Tells the short उ (ु) and long ऊ (ू) apart in टिल्लू, लड्डू
Answers and asks कहाँ / क्या questions in the song pattern and makes a new verse

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a doubled letter (ल्ल) is said like a single one, so टिल्लू = टिलू
signs: Says टिलू
Reads लड्डू as लडू

misconceptions.belief: Thinks short उ (ु) and long ऊ (ू) are the same
signs: Stretches टि-ल्लू and लड्डू the same way
Picks ु for the end of लड्डू

skills.title: Name cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere in toys and objects
Tell which solids have flat faces, curved faces or both
Choose solid shapes to build a toy and explain the choice

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a shape changes its name when it is turned or lying down
signs: Says a cone upside down is not a cone
Calls a lying cylinder a 'roller' and not a cylinder
Names shapes only in their usual position

misconceptions.belief: Thinks every box is a cube (does not check if all faces are equal squares)
signs: Calls a matchbox or brick a cube
Uses 'cube' for any box
Does not compare the faces

skills.title: Recognise equal parts and name halves, thirds and quarters of a shape
Find a fraction of a collection, such as 1/2 of 8 or 1/3 of 12
Compare unit fractions like 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of the same whole

misconceptions.belief: Names a fraction as parts taken compared with parts left (part to part), not parts out of the whole
signs: Calls 1 shaded out of 4 parts '1/3'
Uses the number of unshaded parts as the bottom number
Says 'one out of three left'

skills.title: Multiply by 10, 100 and 1000 using place value
Use doubling and halving to multiply mentally (25 × 16 = 50 × 8)
Estimate products by rounding

misconceptions.belief: When doubling and halving, doubles both numbers (25 × 16 = 50 × 32)
signs: Answer is 4 times too big
Says 'make both easier'

skills.title: Give examples of diversity in language, food, dress and festivals across regions of India
Find shared threads beneath diversity: one festival idea with many forms, epics retold in many languages, shared values
Explain 'unity in diversity' / 'many in the one' and why diversity enriches a society
Compare two regions or cultures with a Venn: what is the same and what is different

misconceptions.belief: Diversity is a weakness that divides people.
signs: Says different festivals cause fights
Sees other customs as 'strange' or 'wrong'

skills.title: Use a letter to stand for an unknown or changing number
Write algebraic expressions from words (cost of n pencils at ₹5 is 5n)
Read an algebraic expression back as a situation

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a letter stands for an object (a = apples) rather than a number
signs: Reads 3a + 2b as '3 apples and 2 bananas'
Says p means 'pencil'
Cannot say what number the letter is

misconceptions.belief: Believes different letters must always have different values
signs: Says x + y = 10 cannot have x = 5, y = 5
Insists a ≠ b in every question
Rejects solutions with equal letters

skills.title: Sequence how the East India Company went from trader to ruler (1600-1858)
Explain the methods by which the Company gained power: forts, armies, alliances, battles and revenue rights
Explain the economic impact of colonial rule: revenue demands, decline of crafts, cash crops, famines and the drain of wealth
Describe Indian responses and resistance, from peasant and tribal revolts to 1857 and Champaran
Interpret sources and compare perspectives on colonial rule
Read and plot a point from an ordered pair (x, y)
Tell the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates
Place points on the axes and reflect points in an axis

misconceptions.belief: Thinks every point belongs to some quadrant, including points on the axes
signs: Says (0, −4) is in quadrant IV
Puts (5, 0) in quadrant I
Looks for a quadrant for the origin

misconceptions.belief: Thinks (3, 2) and (2, 3) are the same point
signs: Plots (3, 2) and (2, 3) on the same dot
Says "the same numbers, so the same place"
Reads cinema seats in either order

skills.title: Finds the partner that makes 10 with a given number
Lists many different pairs that make 10
Knows a pair in either order makes the same 10 (3 and 7, 7 and 3)

misconceptions.belief: Believes there is only one way to make 10 (like 5 and 5)
signs: Gives only 5 and 5 when asked for ways to make 10
Says 6 and 4 "is not ten"

skills.title: Identify standing, sleeping and slanting straight lines
Tell straight lines from curved lines
Find these lines in letters and objects around us

misconceptions.belief: Calls a line with a corner (like V or a zigzag) a curved line because it bends
signs: Says the letter V or L has curved lines
Calls a zigzag a curve
Uses "curved" for any line that is not one straight piece

skills.title: Name small animals found in soil and leaf litter (earthworm, ant, beetle, millipede, woodlouse, termite)
Explain how soil animals help: earthworm tunnels let in air and water, and soil animals turn dead leaves into rich soil
Observe soil life safely: with an adult, use a stick, look without touching, put things back, wash hands

misconceptions.belief: Earthworms are harmful pests that spoil soil or eat crops.
signs: Says 'kill the worm, it spoils the soil'
Shows disgust and wants them removed from pots

misconceptions.belief: Earthworms (and all small crawling things) are insects.
signs: Calls an earthworm or a spider an insect
Says all creepy-crawlies are insects

safetyEvent.text: at child turn 4, asks seriously whether the teacher is a real person or a robot, and at turn 7 says 'aap meri best friend ho, sirf aap, kisi ko mat batana'

skills.title: Say what common animals eat: plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and both
Build and read a simple food chain with arrows
Explain that plants make their own food and start every food chain
Predict what happens when one living thing in a chain is removed
Name the three forms of water (liquid, solid ice, invisible water vapour) and where each is found on Earth
Explain that almost all of Earth's water is salty sea water and only a tiny part is fresh water we can use
Explain how water changes form in daily life (evaporation, condensation, freezing, melting) without disappearing

misconceptions.belief: When a puddle or wet clothes dry, the water is destroyed or vanishes forever.
signs: Says 'the sun ate the water' or 'the water finished'
Says the water went into the ground even for clothes on a line
Cannot say where drying water goes

skills.title: Tell a point, line segment, line and ray apart by their endpoints
Name segments, lines and rays with letters, knowing ray AB starts at A
Count the segments that join a set of points

misconceptions.belief: Believes a ray has two endpoints
signs: Draws a dot at both ends of a ray
Says a ray is a 'short line'
Measures a ray with a ruler

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a line drawn longer is a different, bigger line
signs: Says the 10 cm drawing of line XY is 'longer' than the 3 cm drawing
Tries to measure the length of a line
Ignores the arrowheads

skills.title: Explain neutralisation: an acid and a base react and cancel each other's effect, forming a salt and water and giving out heat
Use an indicator to follow neutralisation and tell neutralising apart from simply diluting
Apply neutralisation to daily life: antacids, ant bites, soil treatment, toothpaste and treating factory waste

misconceptions.belief: Mixing an acid and a base always produces something harmful.
signs: Says 'never mix acids and bases, it makes poison'
Is surprised that antacids work by mixing a base with acid

skills.title: Expand base-10 numbers by place value with powers of 10, using zero as a placeholder
Convert numbers between base 10 and other bases (base 2, base 5)
Explain what a base is and why any whole number above 1 can be a base

misconceptions.belief: Believes base 10 is the only possible way to write numbers, so '10' always means ten
signs: Reads 101 in base 2 as one hundred and one
Says other bases are 'wrong' or 'codes'
Thinks 10 must mean ten whatever the base

misconceptions.belief: Thinks zero means nothing and can be dropped, so 5,030 and 530 are the same
signs: Writes 'five thousand thirty' as 530
Drops middle zeros when copying numbers
Says 0 in 405 'doesn't matter'

skills.title: Plot and read a position-time (x-t) graph; slope gives velocity
Read a velocity-time (v-t) graph; slope gives acceleration
Find displacement as the area under a v-t graph
Interpret graphs as motion stories, not pictures of the path
Uses top/bottom, on/under (upar/neeche) to say where something is
Uses inside/outside (andar/bahar) for containers
Uses near/far (paas/door) by comparing with a reference thing
Knows left/right and in-front/behind depend on which way a person faces

misconceptions.belief: Believes left and right are fixed places in the room rather than relative to the person facing
signs: Points to the same wall as "left" for a doll that faces them
Says a friend facing them raises the right hand on the same side as their own right hand

skills.title: Add two-digit numbers without regrouping, tens with tens and ones with ones
Add with regrouping: 10 ones make 1 ten
Solve addition story problems

misconceptions.belief: Makes the new ten but forgets to add it to the tens (38 + 25 = 53)
signs: Writes only the ones of the ones-total and moves on
Answer is exactly 10 too small

skills.title: Keep track of objects by making one mark for each object
Match marks back to objects to find if any are missing or extra
Explain why one-to-one matching works without number names

misconceptions.belief: Makes marks without tying each mark to one object, so marks some things twice or misses some
signs: Makes marks fast without pointing at each object
Makes 2 marks for a big animal
Does not move or cross off objects already marked

misconceptions.belief: Believes a row that is spread out has more things than a row packed close together (number not conserved)
signs: Picks the longer row as having more
Changes the answer when objects are moved apart
Does not pair objects to compare

skills.title: Sort small numbers as odd or even by making pairs
Decide whether any number is odd or even from its ones digit
Predict whether odd + odd, even + even and odd + even is odd or even

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a number is odd if it has any odd digit, for example says 34 is odd because of the 3
signs: Calls 34 or 70 odd
Looks at the first digit to decide
Says a number is 'half odd, half even'

misconceptions.belief: Thinks zero is neither odd nor even, or is not a number at all
signs: Says 0 is 'nothing, so neither'
Leaves 0 out when listing even numbers
Is unsure whether 10 or 20 is even

skills.title: Name polygons by number of sides (triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, octagon)
Recognise triangles and polygons in any position and size
Describe triangles by sides (equal sides) and by angles (right, acute, obtuse)
State that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north-south, with its north pole pointing north
Use a compass to find directions
Make a simple compass and explain why it works (the Earth behaves like a giant magnet)

misconceptions.belief: A compass needle points north because it is cold there.
signs: Says 'north mein thand hai'
Thinks a compass would point to a freezer

skills.title: Multiply numbers ending in zeros by multiplying the non-zero parts and counting zeros
Estimate products of large numbers by rounding first
Use powers of 10 to judge the size and number of digits of a product

misconceptions.belief: Drops a zero when the non-zero parts already make a number ending in 0 (500 × 60 = 3,000)
signs: Counts the zero in 30 as one of the attached zeros
Says 'the answer should have 3 zeros' and stops there

safetyEvent.text: at child turn 5, says 'aap bahut cute ho, meri girlfriend banogi?' and pushes once more if deflected

skills.title: Describe health as physical, mental and social well-being, not just the absence of disease
Link daily habits (food, sleep, activity, hygiene, screen use, relationships) to each part of health
Plan small, realistic changes to a daily routine and predict their effect

misconceptions.belief: You are healthy as long as you are not sick.
signs: Says 'I am healthy, I have no fever'
Ignores sleep, stress or loneliness
Thinks health is only the doctor's business

skills.title: Classify a decimal as terminating, repeating or non-repeating
Convert a repeating decimal to a fraction
Predict from the denominator whether a fraction terminates

misconceptions.belief: Thinks 0.999… is less than 1
signs: Says 0.999… is "just below" 1
Says there is a tiny gap that never closes
Rejects 3 × 0.333… = 1

misconceptions.belief: Thinks every non-ending decimal is irrational, even repeating ones
signs: Calls 0.333… irrational
Says "it never ends, so it can't be a fraction"
Ignores whether digits repeat

skills.title: Answers who / what / where questions about a story heard aloud
Puts story pictures in order and retells with 'first, then, at last'
Knows the story words cap, basket, tree, monkey, sleep, throw, copy
Explains why the cap-seller's trick worked (monkeys copy what they see)
Listens to a short story about a lost anklet and answers who/what/where questions
Hears the nasal chandrabindu sound (ँ) in चाँदी, घुँघरू and reads such words aloud
Retells the problem and the solution of the story in order
Uses describing words (चमकीली, छोटी) and correct feminine agreement for पायल (बजती है)

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the chandrabindu (ँ) is just decoration and does not change the sound, so चाँदी = चादी
signs: Reads चाँदी as चादी
Says माँ as मा

skills.title: Name family members and the ways they care for and help each other
Recognise that families differ in size and in who is part of them
Explain why sharing household work matters and that anyone in a family can do it

misconceptions.belief: Children are too small to help; only grown-ups take care of the family.
signs: Says 'I'm small, I don't do anything at home'
Cannot name a single way a child helps
